questions.statement: What is the correct structure of the Present Continuous tense in English?
questions.context: In a fifth-grade class in Barranquilla, the teacher explains how to describe what classmates are doing right now.

options.text: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing.
options.feedback: The Present Continuous uses the verb "to be" plus the main verb with -ing.

options.text: Subject + verb in past tense.
options.feedback: The past simple is used for finished actions, not for actions happening now.

options.text: Subject + do/does + verb.
options.feedback: "Do/does" is used in the present simple, not in the continuous.

options.text: Subject + will + verb.
options.feedback: "Will" is used for the future, not for actions happening now.

questions.explanation: Reconocer la estructura del Presente Continuo en inglés: sujeto + am/is/are + verbo en -ing.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does the speaker use "is dancing", "is reading" and "is sleeping"?
questions.context: Read: "Look! Maria is dancing in the living room. Pedro is reading a book, and their dog is sleeping on the sofa."

options.text: Because these actions are happening right now, at the moment of speaking.
options.feedback: The Present Continuous describes actions that are in progress now.

options.text: Because these actions happened a long time ago.
options.feedback: Long ago actions require the past simple, not the continuous.

options.text: Because these actions are planned for next year.
options.feedback: Future plans usually use "going to" or the present continuous with a future time expression.

options.text: Because these actions are general facts, not specific moments.
options.feedback: General facts use the present simple, not the continuous.

questions.explanation: Comprender que el Presente Continuo describe acciones que ocurren en este momento.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is in the Present Continuous and describes an action happening now?
questions.context: A student in Pereira observes the playground and writes: "The children are playing soccer. My friend is eating an apple. Two boys are running very fast."

options.text: The children are playing soccer.
options.feedback: "Are playing" is a correct Present Continuous form for a present action.

options.text: The children plays soccer.
options.feedback: "Plays" is present simple, not continuous, and "children" is plural.

options.text: The children played soccer yesterday.
options.feedback: "Played" is past simple, not continuous.

options.text: The children will play soccer tomorrow.
options.feedback: "Will play" is future simple, not continuous.

questions.explanation: Aplicar la estructura del Presente Continuo para describir acciones del momento.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct Present Continuous answer to the question?
questions.context: At school in Cartagena, a teacher asks: "What are you doing right now? Please answer in English."

options.text: I am writing in my notebook right now.
options.feedback: "Am writing" is the correct Present Continuous form for "I".

options.text: I writes in my notebook right now.
options.feedback: "Writes" is present simple, not continuous.

options.text: I am write in my notebook right now.
options.feedback: After "am" we use the verb in -ing form, not the base form.

options.text: I writing in my notebook right now.
options.feedback: We need the auxiliary "am" plus the verb in -ing.

questions.explanation: Aplicar la conjugación del Presente Continuo con el pronombre "I".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the negative form of the Present Continuous?
questions.context: Read: "Right now, the students are not using their phones in class. They are listening to the teacher and taking notes."

options.text: The students are not using their phones in class.
options.feedback: The negative adds "not" after the verb "to be": are not using.

options.text: The students don't using their phones in class.
options.feedback: "Don't" is used in the present simple, not in the continuous.

options.text: The students not are using their phones in class.
options.feedback: The correct order is "are not using", not "not are using".

options.text: The students is not using their phones in class.
options.feedback: With plural "students" we use "are", not "is".

questions.explanation: Aplicar la forma negativa del Presente Continuo con la posición correcta de "not".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What do Sara and her brother have in common in the text?
questions.context: Compare: "Sara usually walks to school, but today she is walking with her mother because it is raining. Her brother is riding the bus because his bike is broken."

options.text: Both are doing something different from their usual routine right now.
options.feedback: Sara usually walks but is walking with her mother; her brother is riding the bus today.

options.text: Both are doing exactly what they always do.
options.feedback: The text emphasizes changes in their usual routines.

options.text: Neither of them is using any kind of transport.
options.feedback: Both are using transport: walking and riding the bus.

options.text: Both are staying at home today.
options.feedback: The text says they are going to school, not staying at home.

questions.explanation: Analizar acciones presentes que contrastan con rutinas habituales.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you infer about the family from the description?
questions.context: Read: "Right now, my mother is cooking lunch, my father is reading the newspaper, my sister is studying for a test, and I am doing my homework."

options.text: Each member of the family is busy with a different activity at the same time.
options.feedback: The text shows several actions happening at the same moment in the family.

options.text: The whole family is sleeping because no one is doing anything.
options.feedback: Each person is performing an activity, so they are not sleeping.

options.text: Only one person is doing something in the house.
options.feedback: Four different people are doing different activities.

options.text: The family is celebrating a birthday party.
options.feedback: The text describes daily activities, not a birthday party.

questions.explanation: Analizar varias acciones simultáneas usando el Presente Continuo en un mismo contexto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why is the Present Continuous important for real communication in English?
questions.context: Read: 'Using the Present Continuous helps English learners describe what is happening at the moment, share real-time observations and communicate clearly in daily conversations.'

options.text: Because it allows us to describe what is happening right now in daily life and share clear observations with others.
options.feedback: El Presente Continuo es clave para comunicar acciones del momento presente.

options.text: Because it is only used in very formal academic writing.
options.feedback: Se usa en la conversación diaria, no solo en textos académicos formales.

options.text: Because it replaces the present simple in all situations.
options.feedback: El Presente Continuo no reemplaza al simple; ambos cumplen funciones distintas.

options.text: Because it is not useful for talking about the present.
options.feedback: Precisamente, es el tiempo más útil para hablar del presente en curso.

questions.explanation: Evaluar la importancia del Presente Continuo para comunicar acciones del momento en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles
